title: `aliases --check` stops calling an empty cache a missing one (R1005 slice 3)
body:
Slice 3 of `docs/plans/oracle/refuse-on-missing-artifact.md` — **OD-9 / R1005**. Completes R1005.

The predicate changes from contents to existence: `not any(cache_dir.glob("*.json"))` becomes `require_directory(...)`. An empty cache means `fetch` ran and cached nothing — a corpus with no captions, which is a **result**. The report over it is every canonical at zero, `NEVER MATCHED`, and **exit 0**, where before it was exit 1 telling the owner to re-run a stage that had already run.

That the report is *useless* in that state is not a reason to hide it. R1005's point is that it is not a **lie**: the numbers say plainly that nothing was scanned.

`_scan` needed no new branch — it already handles a video with no cached transcript, so an empty cache falls out of the existing path.

The alias table keeps its own wording and its position first, deliberately: no stage produces it (R1007 calls it hand-authored input), so R1005's "name the stage that produces it" has no answer for it.

**One existing test is renamed.** `test_empty_transcript_cache_returns_one_naming_what_to_run` called its state "empty" and it is **absent** — no directory at all. The assertion is unchanged and still passes; the suite now has a separate test for the genuinely empty case, which used to be indistinguishable from it and used to fail.

542 passing.

Carries a merge of the base branch so the required checks run against the tree this will land on.
